originalBehavior: The route is designed as an original longform article that should use the shared Engineering Sandbox shell rather than a bespoke standalone layout.
localStatus: The local route uses the shared Engineering Sandbox longform family with a generated story rail, shared hero framing, and shared footer contract while keeping all public teaching content local to the route.
notes: The route keeps its own Formula 1 visual language through local CSS overrides instead of copying an upstream longform page.
Chapter navigation depends on top-level h1 ids in the longform body.
evidence: The route hero, generated chapter rail, and mobile chapter navigation are all mounted by the shared shell.
The public route uses neutral provenance handling because it is not a vendored replica.

originalBehavior: The route plan calls for an opening scene that lets readers inspect the F1 car as one connected system before drilling into subsystems.
localStatus: The local route ships an interactive car map with component buttons, highlighted regions, and explanatory panel copy for the major aerodynamic, mechanical, braking, and power-unit areas.
notes: This scene is the phase-1 anchor interaction for the route.
The map intentionally prioritizes teaching clarity over geometry accuracy.
evidence: The route ships selectable hotspot buttons and synchronized component copy.
The active component also highlights the matching region in the car diagram.

originalBehavior: The route plan calls for original scenes that explain airflow, ground effect, and braking as connected constraints on lap time.
localStatus: The local route ships simplified airflow, underfloor, and braking scenes with controllable inputs and live derived readouts for load share, drag, stability, suction, platform risk, braking authority, and rotation behavior.
notes: The scenes are intentionally explanatory, not telemetry-grade simulations.
Airflow and underfloor scenes are centered on tradeoffs rather than numeric fidelity.
evidence: Range controls update the scene metrics and illustrations in real time.
The braking scene exposes the stability versus rotation compromise through brake-bias and harvest adjustments.

originalBehavior: The route plan calls for hybrid power, tyre window, track layout, and setup-compromise scenes that bring the article back to lap-time synthesis.
localStatus: The local route ships phase-1 interactions for power mode switching, tyre window management, track archetype selection, and setup-board readouts tied to the active track profile.
notes: Track selection dispatches a shared local event so the setup board can respond to the current circuit profile.
The setup board is a compact synthesis layer for the first shipped phase, not yet a full lap simulator.
evidence: Buttons switch power mode, tyre compounds, and track profiles with updated explanatory copy and metrics.
The setup scene recalculates straight-line speed, slow-corner ability, high-speed support, tyre life, braking confidence, and estimated lap fit.
